attrs.evidence: R5.1 required a conditional ref to RESOLVE, which was the right direction and not far enough. GPT-5.6's audit of R5.1 reported four exploits and all four reproduced against the shipped `consume()`: REPRO-CLOSURE accepted FED-Q2-D3-WITNESS, an existential about girth-4 graphs, as proof that its enumerated import closure covers its domain; FED-PAIRWISE accepted ARG-LED-C9-MEDIATED-SURFACE, an argument about balance mutation in resource.mjs, as its BFMY scope mapping; FED-PAIRWISE accepted a settled claim in place of an argument at all; and FED-PAIRWISE kept its mapping argument while its citation_ref was swapped from BFMY to the valid-but-unrelated Erdos high-girth theorem. A fifth was found reproducing them: an argument written to discharge universal_refutation was accepted for a universal_affirmation. This is the third member of one family — free text is support (R5), a resolving reference is support (R5.1), only a reference ABOUT THIS CLAIM is support (R5.2) — and it is the same distinction OMG SACM 2.3 makes by giving AssertedInference and AssertedEvidence their own identity: a node resolving is not a support relation. Six negative tests, built by mutating the real records rather than by hand-writing fossils.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, round-5.1 audit §2. OMG SACM 2.3 for the AssertedInference/AssertedEvidence separation.
attrs.statement: A conditional support edge is admissible only if the argument it names has the ROLE the consumption rule demands, CONCLUDES that exact claim, DISCHARGES that exact obligation, and — where the rule declares a binding — rests on the source the claim actually cites.
attrs.supersedes: MOS-CONDITIONAL-REF, which stated the resolving half and is retained as the record of that step
